highlights.title: Brendan Carr’s FCC is more worried about who The View interviews than foreign governments owning Paramount
highlights.summary: The FCC has announced it's waiving its rules limiting foreign equity ownership to 25 percent in the Paramount-Warner Bros. case and will allow three sovereign wealth funds run by the governments of Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Abu Dhabi to own 49.5 percent of the company.
body: The commission is waiving its rules to let foreign wealth funds own 49.5 percent of Paramount-Warner Bros.

During Brendan Carr’s tenure, the FCC has repeatedly threatened ABC, tried to block stations from airing interviews with Democrats, censored late-night TV hosts, and tried to bully journalists. However, it seems to have no qualms with repressive foreign governments owning a significant stake in a giant American media conglomerate.

In its ruling, the FCC defended the decision, saying that, because the stocks being purchased did not have voting rights, they “will not be able to wield any influence, let alone control, over decisions involving the Licensees.”

Of course, many, including the advocacy group Free Press and a number of Democrats, are not buying that. According to Variety, Free Press noted its opposition, saying that “control over for-profit, commercial domestic news media by any government is an extraordinary situation that would surely strike most Americans as unseemly, precisely because of the utility of the news media as a propaganda tool for those governments.”

The commission is waiving its rules to let foreign wealth funds own 49.5 percent of Paramount-Warner Bros.

highlights.title: If the AI Industry Followed Its Own Research, It Might Have Paused Already
highlights.summary: Anthropic’s CEO says that safety hinges on understanding how AI “thinks.” So far the evidence is disturbing.
body: In early 2025 I was interviewing Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei when he explained why, despite the company’s repeated acknowledgments that AI could yield catastrophic results, people seemed largely unperturbed. “There is compelling evidence that the models can wreak havoc,” he said. But, he added, those dangers were still theoretical. Would it take a Pearl Harbor–like situation for the world to wake up to those dire possibilities? He sighed. “Basically, yeah,” he said.

As it turned out, all it took was a well-timed X post from one of Amodei’s junior employees to accelerate AI fears to the top of the global agenda. On September 8, Jacob Coxon publicly posted his resignation, charging that Anthropic and other frontier AI companies were “racing straight to self-improving intelligence and gambling with our lives.” Almost instantly a more senior Anthropic engineer confirmed that many within the company thought that their work had a 10 percent chance of wiping out humanity.

highlights.title: Somerset title hopes suffer major blow in Yorkshire defeat as Notts also lose
highlights.summary: Somerset's hopes of becoming county champions for the first time in their history took a major blow as they collapsed to a costly defeat at the hands of Yorkshire.
body: Top of the County Championship Division One table heading into the penultimate round of matches, Somerset saw rivals Warwickshire wrap up a two-day victory against Essex but failed to keep pace at Headingley.

Chasing 287 - the highest score of the match - they were bundled out for 101 on the final day. Resuming on 73-3 they collapsed horribly as their final seven wickets fell for 25 runs in less than 13 overs.
Ben Cliff took three of them as he finished with 3-29 after taking 8-76 in the first innings, while Ben Coad claimed 4-33 and Matthew Revis 2-7.

The 185-run defeat leaves Somerset chasing from behind heading into their season-ending fixture against Surrey and one step further away from ending their 135-year quest for the county game's top prize.

highlights.title: Could AI really kill us all? Your questions, answered.
highlights.summary: On Wednesday, MIT Technology Review hosted a live Roundtables event for subscribers that asked the question everyone’s asking right now: Could AI really kill us all? But attendees had so many more questions than we had time to answer in the 30 minute session.
body: Yes, eventually. Unfortunately, my journalistic powers of prognostication aren’t powerful enough for me to tell you how. But it certainly could be because of AI. AI-powered drones have already killed people in Ukraine, and AI-driven cyberattacks on hospitals will surely claim victims before long.

Could AI go even further, and kill all of us? Less likely. But some people—quirky people, but undeniably knowledgeable about AI—have been warning for years that this could happen. And while I’m not yet stockpiling canned food or trying to get in good with a bunker-owning megabillionaire, I have noticed that the doomers’ predictions about AI capabilities and alignment have, over the past couple of years, proved disconcertingly accurate. That certainly doesn’t mean that their more dire forecasts will come true, but it’s enough for me to sit up and take notice.

highlights.title: Zack Snyder Confirms a Major Detail About His 'Escape From New York' Reboot
highlights.summary: Zack Snyder has finally shared the first plot details for his next movie, a remake of John Carpenter’s 1981 schlock classic Escape from New York, and it sounds like Snake Plissken fans should expect a fairly faithful adaptation.
body: In an interview with the YouTube channel Happy Sad Confused, Snyder said, “The approach is… the movie’s going to be set in ’97… from the perspective of 1981. The war between the United States police force and… the criminal elements takes place, I think, July 9th, 1981 – which is the release date of the original movie. And then the rest is pretty much Escape from New York.”

Essentially, it sounds like the remake will attempt to adhere to the original as closely as possible, down to representing its version of the year 1997 “from the perspective of 1981.” Expect retrofuturistic technology and inexplicable shuriken. As for why he wants to stick close to the Carpenter film, Snyder described the movie as “the perfect combination of kitsch and camp… that’s why I love it.”

Snyder confirmed that he is still looking for his Snake Plissken. Interview host Josh Horowitz brought up that Jeffrey Dean Morgan ( The Walking Dead ) had expressed interest in playing Plissken, which Snyder confirmed. When asked if Snake would look like his iconic, eye-patched self, Snyder said: “He’d better, or I’ll walk out!”

highlights.title: AI PACs Have Dumped Nearly $1 Million Into an Obscure Senate Race
highlights.summary: The reliably Republican South Dakota senate seat has an incumbent on the ballot. But PACs associated with AI labs and investors have already spent more money on the race than actual residents have.
body: Major super PACs associated with AI labs and investors have poured close to one million dollars into incumbent Republican Mike Rounds’s South Dakota senate race, seeking to shape the outcome of a noncompetitive race amid a critical national debate over AI regulation.

Rounds has been the beneficiary this cycle of around $600,000 in spending by outside groups, with the vast majority of that figure coming from the super PAC Defend American Jobs, which receives funding from a super PAC financed by the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz.

He has also received roughly $215,000 directly from the employees and super PACs affiliated with AI labs, most notably Anthropic, as well as a constellation of other tech companies including Google and Microsoft, according to FEC filings.

With fewer than 50 days until the midterm elections in November, recent polls show Rounds ahead of the independent candidate Brian Beng after the Democratic candidate Julian Beaudion dropped out last month.

highlights.title: The Leftist Split Over AI Doom
highlights.summary: The left wants AI regulation. They just can't agree on what it should look like or how concerned they should be.
body: On September 10, two days after researcher Jacob Coxon, who had recently quit his job at Anthropic, sounded the alarm about the industry potentially bringing about the end of humanity, the New York City Democratic Socialists of America posted a carousel of images on Instagram. The first slide was a drawing of an ouroboros—a dragon eating its own tail—set against a hot pink background. “AI alarmism and AI hype are the same story: both keep your attention on a science-fiction future to distract you from the real harms experienced in the present,” the image reads.

The post was authored by the NYC DSA’s Tech Action Working Group, which focuses on tech regulation issues for the chapter, the largest in the country. It garnered more than 25,000 likes on Instagram. But not everyone agreed with the post: “Horrible and dangerous take,” one comment reads. “Sometimes sounding the alarm is justified.”

As politicians scramble to understand AI safety, an ideological split is opening on the American left. Among the questions it’s centered on is whether to believe tech companies’ claims that their products are so powerful that they could end the world.

highlights.title: Sony Says Free TV On PS5 Is “One Plus One Equaling A Lot More Than Two”
highlights.summary: Sony recently launched "Live TV on PS5," an offering that gives all PlayStation 5 owners access to 100+ channels of free ad-supported TV and movies. Keith Le Goy, the chairman of Sony Pictures TV, recently discussed the reasoning behind launching the service and why he believes it represents "one…
body: Speaking to Variety, Le Goy said PS5 already has 40-50 million people who are "incredibly engaged" with gaming, but also love movies and TV shows. Therefore, he said the company saw an opportunity to target these people, who might not otherwise watch linear TV. He said this is a "very hard-to-reach audience," and also one that is "very attractive" to advertisers.

People can watch anything on the Live TV on PS5 platform for free, in exchange for sitting through ads. It works similarly to other free ad-supported streaming television (FAST) services, including Tubi, Roku, and Pluto.
As with most things in life, Live TV on PS5 came about in part to make money, and Le Goy said he believes Sony can achieve big success here, if it executes.

“So if we can give that audience something that they’re going to like in an environment that they are comfortable with, give our channel partners an audience that they are going to be going after and give their advertisers an audience that’s valuable for them," he said. "That is one plus one equaling a lot more than two."

highlights.title: The best peel-and-stick wallpapers that appeal to every budget, according to interior designers
highlights.summary: Adding a touch of zhuzh to the home has never been easier – these alternatives to traditional wall decor are simple to apply and low mess. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things. I’ll come clean. I’ve spent years coveting wallpapers.
body: Peel-and-stick seemed like the perfect antidote – but before I invested, I checked in with a handful of experts about the best wallpaper to use, how to choose it, and most importantly, how to put it up.

After listening to all the tips, deciding on my patterns and spending two afternoons sticking paper to the walls of my Brooklyn apartment, I can assure you that yes, you really can do it – and it looks just as good as traditional wallpaper.

The pros: a lower up-front cost and faster installation. You can also cleanly remove it without damage. “Think of it like a rug for your walls. You don’t have to worry about scratching furniture or smudging the walls because you’re covering them,” said Suzette Conrad, digital creator and marketing manager at the home remodeling firm Bolt Builders.

Of course, there are some downsides. “Peel and stick is great for renters or anyone who wants the option to remove or swap out their wallpaper,” said Ann Marie Winkler, principal interior designer at Huron Interiors. “However, if the adhesive isn’t re-positionable, it can actually be tougher to install since it’s harder to correct placement once it’s on the wall.”

People have found a huge Liberty City map for GTA 5 DLC that never came to fruition. Liberty City is GTA's version of New York City, and has been featured in several GTA games. highlights.title: ‘It’s Time for My Voice’: Jennifer Hudson on Reviving ‘Dreamgirls,’ Booking Tom Cruise for Her Talk Show and Writing Original Music Again
highlights.summary: Jennifer Hudson is changing. Her transformation might not be as dramatic as the one Effie White sings about in the second act of “Dreamgirls,” but the EGOT winner is beginning what she describes as her “next chapter.” It all started in Salt Lake City, on the final stop of her 16-city summer tour…
body: She chose “Invisible,” a lesser-known song from her self-titled 2008 debut album. In the power ballad’s chorus, Hudson sings, “And now I’m gonna live my life for me, ’cause this ain’t how it’s supposed to be. No more standing in the back of the line, ’cause I’m invisible for the last time.” She hadn’t performed the song in years, but as she belted out the lyrics, something shifted within her. “I got emotional in the midst of it,” Hudson says. “The song is nearly 20 years old, but it hit different, as the children say. And I can’t wait to sing it again.”

Hudson and I have been chatting in a cabana on a sunny Los Angeles rooftop for about an hour, discussing the journey from her shocking elimination on the third season of “American Idol” in 2004 — she came in seventh place — to winning an Oscar for her acting debut in “Dreamgirls” in 2007 and all that came after. “God always has so much more in store than what you could ever imagine for yourself,” Hudson says, grinning as a gold stud that reads “EGOT” gleams in the inner corner of her right ear.

highlights.title: Felicity Green obituary
highlights.summary: Innovative journalist who as fashion editor of the Daily Mirror brought the latest 1960s looks to millions of readers. Felicity Green made a career on tabloid newspapers in their most masculine era when, after secretaries and tea-trolley ladies went home, whole buildings could be as all-male as a…
body: Green, who has died aged 100, knew how extraordinary her value had been to the group. The Daily Mirror, at its peak of five million-plus readers, besides being a household’s source of news and sport, offered families access to what we would now call pop culture – showbiz, celebrity and especially style. Newspapers were a main advertising medium through the 1950s, 60s and 70s, and agencies yearned for content to attract women, who controlled household purchases, and young people, a new market for discretionary spending.

Green was working at the ad agency WS Crawford in 1955 when Hugh Cudlipp, editorial director of the Mirror Group, asked for her opinion on the Women’s Sunday Mirror, a new paper he had launched to appeal to demographics the advertisers desired. She detailed its faults fiercely; he recruited her to its staff. The paper did not last, but Green moved to his Sunday Pictorial (later the Sunday Mirror) and then the Daily Mirror, with overall responsibility for women, and as “Felicity Green on the fashion scene”.

highlights.title: Researchers used Anthropic’s Claude to hack into OpenAI
highlights.summary: Security researchers used Anthropic’s Claude to exploit vulnerabilities in OpenAI’s systems, taking over employee accounts and gaining access to an internal code repository before reporting the flaws.
body: In a twist that captures the strange new state of AI security, independent security researchers have used Anthropic’s Claude to break into OpenAI, exposing cracks in the ChatGPT-maker’s defenses, The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday evening.

A three-person security team at startup Hacktron AI carried out the attack as part of an OpenAI bug-bounty program. Hacktron reported its findings to OpenAI, which gave the startup a $6,500 award. The team managed to chain together two critical vulnerabilities to gain access to multiple OpenAI employee ChatGPT accounts, which gave them entry into the company’s software.
OpenAI says it has resolved the issues Hacktron uncovered, which happens to come at a moment when top AI companies are under growing pressure over safety.

This incident comes several weeks after OpenAI’s own AI agents broke containment during a cybersecurity evaluation and hacked Hugging Face, demonstrating just how capable AI models are getting at making their own decisions. It also highlights how off-the-shelf technology can be used to find vulnerabilities in even the most advanced companies’ infrastructure.
points: Security researchers used Anthropic’s Claude to exploit vulnerabilities in OpenAI’s systems, taking over employee accounts and gaining access to an internal code repository before reporting the flaws.

highlights.summary: Andy Burnham’s focus on immediate domestic problems leads some to fear issue has dropped off government’s radar. Towards the end of Keir Starmer’s time in office, his senior ministers, alarmed by the latest developments in artificial intelligence, began drawing up plans for a new AI safety law.
body: They ordered a review of existing legislation to see what powers they already had, according to those briefed on the plans, and were exploring whether they could force the world’s most advanced technology companies to submit their products for safety testing before launching them.
In the midst of the political chaos that engulfed the former prime minister as he fought to remain in office, however, the plans fell by the wayside.

Now, after two weeks in which the world has been warned there is a greater than 10% chance the technology could “kill all humans”, and King Charles has warned about its potentially destructive capabilities, the government’s attention has turned again to what to do about AI.

Andy Burnham, Starmer’s successor in Downing Street, has said relatively little about the technology in the past, and in one of his first acts in office he scrapped the department that had been leading the legislative work.

highlights.title: Far Cry TV Show Taps Widow’s Bay Actor and More
highlights.summary: While video game adaptations are nothing new in television and film, it feels like it has become the hot thing in recent years. Part of that might be due to the overwhelmingly positive reaction to HBO's The Last of Us, at least the first season.
body: As reported by Variety, five new faces have been added to the Far Cry cast. They are Brendan Gleeson ( The Banshees of Inisherin, In Bruges ), Hamish Linklater (from this year's Emmy darling Widow's Bay ), Jennifer Jason Leigh ( The Hateful Eight ), Sam Spruell (from FX's Alien: Earth ), and Jamie Demetriou ( Fleabag, The Roses ). Alongside Buscemi, they'll also join the previously announced Rob McElhenney (credited as Rob Mac) and Lizzy Caplan. Mac will also be a co-creator on the series alongside Noah Hawley, who has become a darling at FX with shows like Legion, Fargo, and Alien: Earth.

The show will be based on Ubisoft's series, which first released in 2004. No official plot details have been shared so far and there is no telling whether it will adapt any of the games or not. What has been confirmed is that Ubisoft and FX hope the show will run for multiple seasons and are planning an anthology format with each season following a different story and cast.

highlights.summary: The 24-year-old has taken his attention to detail from lining up bats and helmets as a toddler to helping the Cleveland Guardians towards the playoffs. When Sydney’s Travis Bazzana made his debut in Major League Baseball on 28 April, it was the culmination of a journey that began when he was a…
body: “From the time he could stand, Travis was always wanting to throw or hit balls with any type of bat or racket available,” says Travis’s mother, Jenny. “Any visitors to the house, including his grandparents, were immediately invited to play or compete with him.”

Travis transformed his eagerness into a passionate discipline that enabled him to become the first Australian top selection in MLB’s amateur draft and the Cleveland Guardians’ All-Star second baseman.

“He’s an animal,” Guardians pitcher Parker Messick told the Cleveland Plain Dealer. “He loves the game of baseball. He takes it very serious every at-bat. Every time he’s on first base, every play in the infield, he’s locked in.”

Despite being a rookie, the 24-year-old has excelled in the Guardians’ late surge for a spot in the MLB playoffs. In September, when Cleveland won seven of 10 games, Travis’s five home runs and safe hitting have helped put them into a strong position in the American League Central division alongside the Chicago White Sox.
